andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh gazettes reconstitution of Zilla Praja Parishads for its 28 districts
facts: G.O.Ms.No.116 was issued on 2026-09-05 by the Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department (MDL-II).
The Andhra Pradesh Gazette published the reconstitution notification on 2026-09-07.
The notification covers all 28 districts and reorganizes the existing 13 Zilla Praja Parishads.
The order is a fresh formal notification in the continuing Zilla Praja Parishad reconstitution process.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: Zilla Praja Parishad reconstitution had been covered earlier. Today: G.O.Ms.No.116 was published in the Andhra Pradesh Gazette, formally notifying reconstitution corresponding to all 28 districts and reorganizing the existing 13 Parishads. The Gazette notice is the new development; it does not by itself establish that every administrative transition is complete.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: 73rd Constitutional Amendment; three-tier Panchayati Raj and district-level local self-government.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the distinction between the 28-district coverage in the notification and the 13 existing Zilla Praja Parishads it reorganizes.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how district reorganization affects the territorial alignment, representation and administrative capacity of rural local bodies.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP link: G.O.Ms.No.116 reorganizes the state's Zilla Praja Parishads to correspond with Andhra Pradesh's 28 districts.

# 1. Gazette notification
- **What:** Fresh formal notification for reconstitution of **Zilla Praja Parishads (ZPPs)** in **Andhra Pradesh**
- **Issued by:** **G.O.Ms.No.116**, **Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department (MDL-II)**, on **2026-09-05**
- **Published:** **Andhra Pradesh Gazette**, **2026-09-07**

| Basis | Number | Significance |
|---|---:|---|
| District coverage | **28 districts** | Reconstitution corresponds to all districts |
| Existing Parishads | **13 Zilla Praja Parishads** | Existing Parishads are reorganized |

- **Status:** Gazette notification issued as part of the continuing reconstitution process; it does **not** establish that every administrative transition is complete
- **Background:** **73rd Constitutional Amendment**; **three-tier Panchayati Raj** and district-level local self-government [GK]
- ⚠ **Trap:** Distinguish the notification's coverage of **28 districts** from the **13 existing Zilla Praja Parishads** being reorganized.
> Exam angle: Test the Gazette notification's issuing department and the distinction between district coverage and existing Parishad count.

andhraPradesh.headline: New NTR Bharosa pension application window opens across Andhra Pradesh
facts: Fresh applications under the NTR Bharosa Pension Scheme are being accepted from 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-16.
Applications are to be received through Swarna Gramam and Swarna Ward centres across the state.
The application intake is followed by scrutiny and verification; applying does not itself confer pension eligibility or approval.
The scheme provides social-security pensions to eligible older people, widows, persons with disabilities and other covered categories.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: The September application window had been announced. Today: the application period opened, with eligible residents able to submit applications at designated Swarna Gramam and Swarna Ward centres through 2026-09-16. Pension sanction remains subject to eligibility checks and verification.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Social security and welfare delivery; targeted assistance and last-mile public service administration.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The application window is 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-16; distinguish application intake from verification and final sanction.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how accessible application channels and transparent verification can widen social-protection coverage while reducing exclusion and inclusion errors.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh reviews 1,162.8 MW of PM-KUSUM feeder-level solar projects
facts: Andhra Pradesh is taking up 1,162.8 MW of feeder-level solarisation through 228 solar power plants under PM-KUSUM Component C.
Energy Special Chief Secretary K. Vijayanand reviewed implementation with state distribution companies and officials on 2026-09-07.
Land acquisition was reported complete for all 228 plants; civil works, equipment procurement, financial closure and statutory documentation remain implementation-monitoring priorities.
The state set a target to commission 109.7 MW during September and October 2026; this is a target, not completed capacity.
The projects are intended to support renewable generation and daytime electricity supply to agricultural feeders.

andhraPradesh.headline: Railway Gazette notification designates competent authorities for Nidadavolu–Duvvada third and fourth lines
facts: A Ministry of Railways notification under Section 2(7A) of the Railways Act, 1989, concerns the 198.10-km third and fourth lines between Nidadavolu and Duvvada.
The Gazette notification designates Revenue Divisional Officers as competent authorities for specified project areas in East Godavari and Anakapalli districts.
The designated authorities include the RDOs at Rajamahendravaram, Anakapalli and Adduroad Junction for the listed mandals.
The notification authorizes competent-authority functions for project execution, maintenance, management and operation; it is not evidence that the rail lines are completed.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh cities and wards feature in the 5th Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards
facts: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change conferred the 5th Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards on 7 September 2026, under the National Clean Air Programme.

The assessment covered 130 cities in three population categories; city performance was evaluated on air-quality management measures including road dust, waste management, vehicle and industrial emissions, and public outreach.
In the category for cities with populations above 10 lakh, Vijayawada ranked 8th with a score of 186 and Visakhapatnam ranked 21st with a score of 172.
In the 3–10 lakh category, Guntur ranked 2nd with a score of 195; Nellore ranked 9th, Rajahmundry 14th and Kurnool 29th.
In the below-3-lakh category, Eluru ranked 4th, Vizianagaram 6th, Srikakulam 11th, Ongole 25th and Chittoor 26th.
Vijayawada Ward 60 ranked 2nd nationally in the 10,000–30,000 population ward category.
Andhra Pradesh’s state-level ward awardees included Guntur Ward 42 in category 2, Vijayawada Ward 31 in category 3 and Nellore Ward 06 in category 3.
andhraPradesh.summary: The fifth Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan awards recognised city and ward performance in air-quality management. Andhra Pradesh had multiple city placements and ward awardees, including Vijayawada’s second-place national ward ranking in its population category.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: MoEFCC conferred the 5th Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards on 7 September 2026. Andhra Pradesh awardees included Vijayawada Ward 60 (national rank 2 in its ward category), Guntur Ward 42, Vijayawada Ward 31 and Nellore Ward 06.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Use the state’s city and ward results to discuss local-body capacity, citizen participation and evidence-based interventions under the National Clean Air Programme.

national.headline: Defence Acquisition Council grants in-principle approval for proposals worth about ₹1.10 lakh crore
facts: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, granted Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) on 7 September 2026.
The proposals have an estimated value of about ₹1.10 lakh crore; AoN is in-principle administrative approval, not a completed procurement.
Army proposals include CBRN reconnaissance vehicles, high-mobility vehicles, advanced light helicopters, trawl tanks and the Sarvatra Bridge System.
Navy proposals include Arudhra radars and design, development and subsequent procurement of marine gas turbines.
Air Force proposals include a Ground-Based Multi-Purpose Jammer and the Defence Forces Secure Access Card system.
About 98% of the approved procurement is to be sourced from Indian industry.
national.summary: The DAC granted AoN to defence acquisition proposals estimated at about ₹1.10 lakh crore across the Army, Navy and Air Force. The 98% Indian-industry sourcing share supports the defence indigenisation objective, but AoN is an initial approval and does not mean contracts have been awarded or equipment delivered.
national.staticLink: Defence Acquisition Procedure; capital procurement; Aatmanirbhar Bharat in defence.
national.prelimsTakeaway: AoN means Acceptance of Necessity and is an in-principle administrative approval; it is not a final purchase contract.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how defence procurement can balance operational readiness, domestic manufacturing, technology absorption and fiscal prudence.

national.headline: NITI Aayog launches PACT and Zero Emission Truck Marketplace
facts: NITI Aayog Member Rajiv Gauba launched the Platform for Aggregating Clean Transport (PACT) at the 5th e-FAST India Summit 2026.
PACT is designed to aggregate freight demand from shippers, logistics service providers and other stakeholders, supporting deployment opportunities along freight corridors.
The summit also introduced the Zero Emission Truck (ZET) Marketplace, connecting truck makers, logistics firms, charging operators, financiers and technology companies.

The PIB release reported that e-freight vehicle deployments increased from 201 in FY 2024–25 to 826 in FY 2025–26, and that more than 3,000 electric medium- and heavy-duty trucks were operating nationally.
The platforms aim to improve demand visibility, charging-infrastructure planning and the commercial case for zero-emission freight.
The 5th e-FAST India Summit was convened under the NITI Aayog-led e-FAST India platform at The Ashok, New Delhi; its theme was “Moving from Market Creation to Market Transformation.”
national.summary: NITI Aayog launched PACT and the ZET Marketplace to coordinate demand, finance, charging and commercial partnerships for zero-emission freight. The initiative is a market-coordination platform; it does not itself amount to a commitment to purchase or deploy a specified number of trucks.
national.staticLink: Electric mobility; freight-sector decarbonisation; NITI Aayog and public-private coordination.
national.prelimsTakeaway: PACT stands for Platform for Aggregating Clean Transport; ZET refers to the Zero Emission Truck Marketplace introduced at the 5th e-FAST India Summit.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how demand aggregation, corridor planning and access to finance can address barriers to decarbonising heavy freight while safeguarding logistics competitiveness.

national.headline: 28th Western Zonal Council meeting held in Panaji
facts: The 28th Western Zonal Council meeting was chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Panaji, Goa, on 7 September 2026.
Participants included the Chief Ministers of Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra and the Administrator of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
The Western Zonal Council comprises Goa, Gujarat, Maharashtra and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
The councils are established under Sections 15–22 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956; the Union Home Minister chairs the Western Zonal Council.
The PIB account said 1,893 issues had been discussed in Zonal Council and Standing Committee meetings, of which 1,445 were resolved.
The meeting discussed monitoring issues, implementation of the new criminal laws and linking urban cooperative banks with the CFCFRMS.
national.summary: Previous: the 28th Western Zonal Council meeting was announced for 7 September in Panaji. Today: the meeting convened, bringing the member States and Union Territory together to review regional and implementation issues. Andhra Pradesh is not a member of this council.
national.staticLink: Inter-State Council and Zonal Councils; cooperative federalism; States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The Western Zonal Council includes Goa, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu; it is constituted under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the role and limitations of Zonal Councils as forums for cooperative federalism and intergovernmental coordination.

national.headline: Centre reviews plan to upgrade 300 Krishi Vigyan Kendras and establish incubation centres
facts: The Union Agriculture Minister reviewed the action plan for strengthening Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) through greater State participation.
The plan targets infrastructure and logistics upgrades at 300 prioritised KVKs by March 2027.
Incubation-cum-Skill Centres are targeted in all KVKs by December 2028.
States are being asked to support implementation and help mobilise funding through State institutions and agricultural universities.
The review also discussed KVK staffing, timely fund flows and support for district-specific activities under the Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana.
For the 2026–27 Cluster Frontline Demonstrations on pulses and oilseeds, activities were reported across 24 States through 353 KVKs or districts.
national.summary: The Centre reviewed implementation planning for KVK infrastructure upgrades and incubation-cum-skill centres, with delivery dependent on State participation and funding support. The release records targets and a review, not completion of the upgrades.

national.headline: Clean Air for Blue Skies Day: India reports PM10 reductions in 108 NCAP cities
facts: The International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies is observed on 7 September; the UN General Assembly designated it in 2019.
India observes the occasion as Swachh Vayu Diwas.
The National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) covers 130 cities, according to the PIB backgrounder.
For FY 2025–26, 108 cities recorded lower PM10 levels than in 2017–18.
Of those 108 cities, 72 recorded reductions above 20% and 26 recorded reductions above 40%.
As of March 2026, India’s ambient air-quality monitoring network comprised 1,646 stations across 603 cities in 28 States and 7 Union Territories.

For 2026, UNEP framed the International Day of Clean Air for blue skies around integrated climate and clean-air action for healthier populations and shared prosperity; the Asia-Pacific commemoration used the theme “Clean Air for Climate Action.”
national.summary: On the annual clean-air observance, the government highlighted NCAP coverage and reported city-level PM10 reductions against the 2017–18 baseline. The figures concern PM10 trends and should not be read as evidence that all pollutants or all cities met national air-quality standards.
national.staticLink: Air pollution; PM10 and PM2.5; National Clean Air Programme; ambient air-quality monitoring.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies falls on 7 September; NCAP is India’s city-focused clean-air programme.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the public-health and governance challenges of air pollution, including monitoring, source-specific controls and coordination across jurisdictions.

national.headline: Government backgrounder highlights jute output, exports and livelihoods in FY 2025–26
facts: A PIB backgrounder released on 7 September 2026 reported raw jute and mesta production of 94.03 lakh bales in FY 2025–26, against 88.02 lakh bales in FY 2024–25.
India produced 12.80 lakh metric tonnes of jute goods in FY 2025–26; domestic consumption was 12.05 lakh metric tonnes.
Exports in FY 2025–26 included 22,700 tonnes of raw jute worth ₹225.11 crore and 1,71,300 tonnes of jute goods worth ₹3,155.27 crore.
The backgrounder reported that jute cultivation supports nearly 40 lakh farm families and the organised mills and diversified units employ about 3.70 lakh workers.
Jute and mesta are grouped as raw jute in trade and industrial use; jute is known as the Golden Fibre.

international.headline: UNEP–CCAC assessment says integrated clean-air and climate action could return US$15 per dollar invested
facts: UNEP and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC) released Hidden Assets: The Economic and Health Case for Climate and Clean Air Action on 7 September 2026.
The assessment estimates that each US$1 invested in combined climate and clean-air measures could generate about US$15 in economic benefits.
Its package covers 25 measures across energy, industry, transport, agriculture and food, residential cooking and heating, and waste management.
The modeled annual benefits equal 2.8% of global GDP in 2035, 4.5% in 2050 and 11.4% in 2100.
The report estimates that delaying action by a year would forgo more than US$1.5 trillion in annual combined benefits.
The report was released on the International Day of Clean Air for blue skies; its findings are relevant to India’s air-quality and climate-policy challenges.
international.summary: UNEP and CCAC published a global economic assessment arguing that tackling air pollution and climate change together can yield greater benefits than addressing them separately. Its estimates connect clean-air policy with public health, productivity and climate mitigation, making integrated planning a key policy lesson. No direct AP-specific link established.
international.staticLink: Air pollution, climate change, sustainable development and international environmental cooperation
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the report title, its publishers (UNEP and CCAC), and its headline estimate: around US$15 in benefits for every US$1 invested in integrated climate and clean-air action.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how coordinated air-quality, health, energy and climate policies can generate co-benefits, and discuss institutional and financing barriers to implementation.

international.headline: 2026 Balzan Prizes announced across digital technology, molecular evolution, Jewish studies and biodegradable polymers
facts: The International Balzan Foundation announced the 2026 Balzan Prize winners in Milan on 7 September.

Elena Esposito won for the social science of digital technology; Rasmus Nielsen and Ziheng Yang for molecular evolution; David Nirenberg for Jewish studies; and Geoffrey W. Coates and Marc A. Hillmyer for biodegradable polymers from renewable sources.
Sudan’s Emergency Response Rooms received the 2026 Prize for Humanity, Peace and Fraternity among Peoples.
Each prize carries 750,000 Swiss francs; half of each annual prize must support research projects conducted by young scholars and scientists.
The 2026 prizes are scheduled to be presented in Rome on 19 November.
international.summary: The 2026 Balzan awards recognized work spanning digital technology, genomics, Jewish studies, sustainable materials and humanitarian response. The prize structure links international recognition with support for research by early-career scholars and scientists. No direct AP-specific link established.

international.headline: UN observes International Day of Police Cooperation under the theme of trust and legitimacy
facts: The United Nations observed the International Day of Police Cooperation on 7 September 2026.
The 2026 theme was “Protecting against Vulnerability – Building Trust and Legitimacy in Policing.”
The UN General Assembly established the annual observance through resolution 77/241, adopted in 2022.
The observance highlights international cooperation in support of national police and law-enforcement agencies, including cross-border collaboration and accountable, rights-based policing.
international.summary: The UN observance highlighted how international police cooperation can support responses to cross-border threats while strengthening public trust and institutional legitimacy. Its 2026 theme links effective policing with protection of vulnerable people, accountability and respect for human rights. No direct AP-specific link established.
